configuration: One epoch2d build; the official field-only Maxwell-solver deck epoch2d/tests/maxwell_solvers/pukhov/input.deck run on four ranks laid out 2 by 2 at its upstream 240 x 80 cells and its upstream 75 fs window, with a CPML laser boundary at x_min, CPML outflow at x_max and periodic transverse boundaries. The deck selects the Pukhov (NDF) stencil through its own maxwell_solver key, which is what makes it a different official test from the Yee deck: the stencil is wider, so the guard region the exchange has to fill is wider too and EPOCH raises the number of guard cells to match. It adds explicit nproc keys and use_pre_balance = F, balance_first = F so the partition is exactly the one mpi_routines.F90 computes, and enables the output lines the upstream file leaves commented out so that all the field components the solver advances are graded. Graded (new physical contract): only the assembled global physical outputs named in comparison.files are checked (ex, ey, bz, field_energy); coordinate-indexed SDF arrays use x-fastest, then y, then z, and global species counts, where present, are exact little-endian int64 values. MPI layout controls are execution context only: rank identifiers, boundaries, local counts, ownership/order, repartition or load ladders, schedules and timing are explicitly ungraded.
variant: the laser intensity_w_cm2 of the deck multiplied by (1 + 1e-15). The deck parser evaluates 1.0e15 to 1000000000000001.1, an absolute change of 1.125 where one unit in the last place of binary64 at that magnitude is 0.125, so the perturbation is nine units in the last place, applied to one initial-condition value. It changes the round-off path of the whole field advance without changing the physics, so the physical arrays listed in comparison.files differ and their distance is the round-off floor of this policy. This nominal-versus-variant input is a controlled numerical-sensitivity probe only: it does not change the current provisional bounds or establish acceptance for a new science run. The pointwise policy grades only the physical outputs named by this rubric; execution layout, rank identifiers, boundaries, local counts, ownership/order, repartition schedule and timing are not grading targets.

warrant: The halo-pukhov-2d contract grades only ex, ey, bz, field_energy. The pointwise policy is appropriate because the accepted target is each assembled physical array at its canonical coordinate (and the layout check additionally records a physical zero delta). The original-head source rationale identifies EPOCH's dimension-appropriate boundary/halo exchange and Maxwell field-stencil path (with explicit epoch2d/src/boundary.F90:222-315 and epoch3d/src/boundary.F90:346-449 references where applicable). Those source mechanisms determine the assembled global physical field; a stale guard value, wrong pass ordering or missing physical boundary update would change the field near a seam. A correct implementation must therefore produce finite, shape-compatible assembled SDF values and the listed global physical reductions; differences in rank metadata or execution bookkeeping cannot substitute for a physical result and are not graded. Fresh identical-physics MPI-layout calibration measured maximum pointwise field difference 0.0002560615539550781; the accepted effective coordinate-indexed atol floor is 0.0025 with rtol 1e-08. The user accepted these measured bounds on 2026-09-12. Historical evidence from original head af86f6c6da61b5efbcbb8d5e908950f73b65608f is retained in evidence for measured runtime, native alternative-build behavior and prior bound derivations. It is archival provenance only; the fresh 2026-09-12 calibration above is the current tolerance evidence.
